'''Ruth Heller''' ({{Langx|he|רות הלר}}) is an Israeli statistician and professor at [[Tel Aviv University]]. Heller focuses on diverse areas of statistics and biostatistics, including multiple comparisons, selective inference, conformal inference, and study reproducibility.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Siegfried |first1=Tom |title=Reproducing experiments is more complicated than it seems |url=https://www.sciencenews.org/blog/context/reproducing-experiments-more-complicated-it-seems |access-date=21 February 2025 |agency=Science News |date=21 February 2025}}</ref>

She earned a BSc in mathematics from [[McGill University]] in 1996, and a MSc in biostatistics from the [[University of Washington]] in 1998.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Rousseeuw Prize 2024 Presentation |journal=IMS Bulletin |volume=54 |issue=1 |url=https://imstat.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Bulletin54_1.pdf}}</ref> She earned a PhD from Tel Aviv University in 2007. Her advisors were [[Yoav Benjamini]] and Felix Abramovich.

She was a visiting lecturer at the University of Pennsylvania from 2007 to 2009. In 2011, she joined the Department of Statistics and Operations Research at Tel Aviv University as a senior lecturer. In 2016, she was appointed associate professor, and in 2021, she was appointed full professor.

==Honors and awards==
Together with Yoav Benjamini and [[Daniel Yekutieli]], she won the [[Rousseeuw Prize for Statistics]] in 2024 "for the pioneering work on the [[false discovery rate]] and methods to control it".<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Rousseeuw Prize for Statistics |url=https://www.rousseeuwprize.org/news/winners-2024 |access-date=2024-08-01 |website=www.rousseeuwprize.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Fiske |first1=Gavriel |title=Tel Aviv University team wins international $1 million statistics prize |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/tel-aviv-university-team-wins-international-1-million-statistics-prize/ |access-date=21 February 2025 |work=[[The Times of Israel]] |agency=The Times of Israel |issn=0040-7909}}</ref>
